page.title: Best 2000Wh Power Station Under $600 (2026): What Each Delivers at the Outlet
page.h1: Best 2000Wh power station under $600: what each one delivers at the outlet
page.desc: The FOSSiBOT F2400 is the 2,048 Wh LiFePO4 station that fits a $600 budget. Named tests got 1,512 to 1,659 Wh from its AC outlets. Four stations compared.
page.answer: Short answer. The best 2048Wh LiFePO4 portable power station under $600 in November 2026 is the FOSSiBOT F2400 on Amazon ($669 at FOSSiBOT's own store). Named tests got 1,512 to 1,659 Wh from its AC outlets, 74-81% of the label.

cells.price: Off Anker's US store: its F2000 page now shows the C2000 Gen 2 (maker, 2026-11-11)

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • FOSSiBOT F2400, share of the label: 1,512 ÷ 2,048 = 74% (Techtest, 100 W AC load) and 1,659 ÷ 2,048 = 81% (nextpit).
  • Hours at a 100 W AC load: 1,512 Wh ÷ 100 W = 15.1 hours, against 2,048 ÷ 100 = 20.5 hours if you size from the label.
  • What a $600 budget buys per delivered Wh: $600 ÷ 2,048 = $0.293 per rated Wh, but $600 ÷ 1,659 = $0.362 and $600 ÷ 1,512 = $0.397 per Wh that reached the outlet. At FOSSiBOT's own store price of $669 that is $669 ÷ 1,512 = $0.442.
  • Anker SOLIX F2000 against the F2400: 1,800 − 1,659 = 141 Wh to 1,870 − 1,659 = 211 Wh more per charge, in a unit that is 67.2 − 48.5 = 18.7 lb heavier.
  • Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 at its maker price: $999 ÷ 1,740 Wh = $0.574 per delivered Wh, for the lightest unit here at 38.9 lb.
  • BLUETTI Elite 200 V2: 1,910 ÷ 2,073.6 = 92% of the label, the highest share in this group.

What each 2 kWh station delivered at the outlet

The capacity on the box is the energy in the cells. What reaches an appliance is lower, because the inverter that makes 120 V AC uses power the whole time it is on. Techtest (Michael Barton) shows the size of that loss on the F2400: the same 100 W load drew 1,807 Wh over USB-C but 1,512 Wh from the AC outlet, a 295 Wh difference. Over the 15.1-hour AC run that is 295 ÷ 15.1 = about 19.5 W of extra loss with the inverter running. A light load is the worst case, since that overhead is a large share of 100 W.

FOSSiBOT's own FAQ sizes runtime as watt-hours × 0.85 ÷ device watts, so the maker's planning figure is 2,048 × 0.85 = 1,741 Wh, or 17.4 hours at 100 W. Both named tests came in below it: 1,512 Wh (Techtest) and 1,659 Wh (nextpit, Thomas Kern, load not stated). nextpit also metered 2,127 Wh from the wall for a full charge, so 1,659 ÷ 2,127 = 78% round trip, and a 2.5-hour charge against the maker's 2-hour claim. Techtest timed about 2 h 45 min at the 1,100 W setting.

The Anker SOLIX F2000 delivered about 1,800 Wh over a good 7 hours at roughly 250 W (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten) and 1,870 Wh before inverter cutoff (StorageReview, Jordan Ranous). It took 2,300 to 2,309 Wh to refill, and Notebookcheck timed a full charge at just under 1.5 hours. The Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 gave 1,740 Wh in OutdoorGearLab's text and 1,710 Wh in its spec table (Chris McNamara and Kenji Mowrey), with a 2.5-hour charge. The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 discharged 1.91 kWh and needed 2.44 kWh to recharge (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty): 1.91 ÷ 2.44 = 78% round trip.

These tests used different loads and labs, and Techtest, nextpit and Notebookcheck tested 230 V European units, so read the gaps as indicative. The ranking still holds across them: the F2400 delivers the smallest share of its label of the four.

No 2,000 Wh-class station is under $600 on its maker's own US store today. Prices read on 2026-11-11:

An F2000 priced inside this budget therefore comes from a marketplace seller: ask who honors the 5-year warranty before paying. Not recommended

DYNESS 2048Wh 2400W. It is the lowest-priced 2,048 Wh listing we checked on Amazon on 2026-11-11, but the listing's 2,048 Wh is the only capacity figure available: no named reviewer has metered what it delivers, and we could cite no maker US product page with a warranty term. With the F2400 delivering 74 to 81% of the same label, an untested label is not a basis for a pick.

A Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 offered inside this budget. Jackery's own store has it at $999 on pre-order, so any offer at $600 or less is at least $999 − $600 = $399 below the maker. Treat that as a seller-risk purchase and check the return policy and who provides the warranty first.
